newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Apr 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Apr 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office issued a public consultation paper on proposed legal changes tightening civil liberties by restricting demonstrations and banning foreign donations to local political parties.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Governor Chris Patten criticised the proposed changes to the Public Order and Societies Ordinances. He urged the Chief Executive-designate to reflect Hong Kong people's wishes to Beijing after the consultation was completed.

-- Democratic Party chairman Martin Lee said the proposal restricting foreign donations to local political parties showed that the Chief Executive-designate and the provisional legislature were afraid of his party.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng said that China had a huge market of US$700 billion and urged foreign investors to grab the golden chance to enter China.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Shanghai Industrial Holdings, the trading arm of the Shanghai municipal government, raised HK$4.77 billion through a share placement to finance its acquisition of a 35 percent interest in two roads in Shanghai.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Hong Kong Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement in China, which has been branded subversive by Beijing, said the proposed change to the two rights ordinances slid open the door for action against the alliance.
-- A confidential report by the head of the International Monetary Fund warned that confidence in the future of Hong Kong was the key to its economic prospects after the handover.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinse Premier Li Peng said that China's year-on-year retail inflation rate might fall to as low as three percent in the first quarter of the year.
